parsed.title: Discussion on AI tools, job search, and code quality

topics.title: Automation of job search and resume generation

claims.text: P1 is preparing for a full‑time job search and plans to set up cloud automation for generating PDF resumes tailored to specific vacancies.
P5 plans to wait for their startup to close to have free time to configure OpenClaw for finding vacancies, generating resumes, and writing cover letters.
P6 states that in 2026 job seekers need many AI‑related skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, Embeddings, etc.) to avoid being filtered out by recruiters.
P8 claims that lack of AI knowledge makes job searching for JS/Python positions very difficult in the current market.
P14 expects the recruiter profession to become extinct.
P15 describes passing an Angular interview despite the HR not reading the resume and the vacancy missing the resume requirement.

topics.title: Perception and usage of AI tools in 2024‑2026

claims.text: P7 humorously contrasts attitudes toward AI in 2024 and 2026.
P9 says the acceleration of development by AI started in 2025, with tools becoming sufficiently good but increasingly expensive.
P10 likens current AI tooling to the evolution of REST, JSON, Microservices, Docker after React.
P11 notes that despite the passage of time, nothing has fundamentally changed.
P13 observes that candidate‑search keywords are more detached from reality than before.

topics.title: AI’s effect on software development speed and quality

claims.text: P19 reports that using GPT to generate SQL joins and other code drastically speeds up development, eliminating routine tasks.
P20 suggests exporting logs to JUnit to catch recurring issues earlier.
P21 claims that people are unable to improve because they are “stupid” and incapable of learning.
P22 states that answer quality is often proportional to question quality and the amount of additional knowledge available to the system.
P24 echoes that the quality of a response depends on the quality of the question and the system’s knowledge.
P30 argues that AI lowers the entry barrier to programming, leading to poorly optimized code (e.g., massive generated SQL queries).
P34 mentions that incremental computations have been buried and replaced with a “view” memorial.
P35 describes a case where AI‑generated code (SELECT *) was pushed to production without review, causing problems.

topics.title: Issues with AI‑generated code and code review

claims.text: P35 recounts a situation where an AI‑generated feature broke the project and was ultimately discarded after code review.
P30 provides an example of an AI‑generated 450‑line raw SQL query that retrieves excessive data and creates non‑optimal queries in production.
